correctness.rationale: Independently enumerated all 2047 vertex subsets under quadratic-residue tournament orientation: face vector (11,55,110,55), affine maps 55, translation11 and multiplier5 all preserve order. Every transitive simplex stabilizer fixes vertices, so topological quotient is an orbit CW complex with well-defined signed cellular differentials. Fresh independent integral Smith forms: G cells (1,1,2,1), d2=(1,1), d3=(-2,2)^T, quotient ≃ Moore M(Z/2,2) after collapsing degree-one 1/2-cell pair; T cells (1,5,10,5), SNF d2=(1,1,1,1,11), d3=(1,1,1,1,2), yielding H1 Z/11 and H2 Z/2; H cells (3,11,22,11), SNF d1=(1,1),d2=1^9,d3=1^10,2, yielding H2 Z²⊕Z/2. Chain compositions verified, and rational fixed-cell character confirmed.
residual_risks: Exact finite verification cannot imply an unasserted parametrized generalization; all conclusions bounded as stated.

value.rationale: The unique natural 55-element affine symmetry of the smallest known directed-flag Moore-torsion tournament yields unexpectedly torsion-bearing and homotopically rigid orbit spaces. Exact G,T,H comparison refines Govc’s known nonequivariant X decomposition and provides a concrete test of integral torsion under finite topological quotients, not routine group averaging.
